privileged_mode_enabled.title: Privileged Mode Enabled
privileged_mode_enabled.description: Indicates whether the container is launched with the --privileged flag, granting full host capability sets and disabling seccomp, AppArmor/SELinux enforcement, and most capability restrictions.

granted_capabilities.title: Granted Linux Capabilities
granted_capabilities.description: List of Linux capabilities explicitly granted to the container beyond the default set (e.g., CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_ADMIN).

capability_drop_all_enforced.title: All Default Capabilities Dropped
capability_drop_all_enforced.description: Whether the container configuration explicitly drops ALL capabilities before selectively re-adding only required ones (drop: [ALL] pattern). True means the least-privilege baseline is enforced.

seccomp_profile_type.title: Seccomp Profile Type
seccomp_profile_type.description: The type of seccomp profile applied to the container or pod. 'Unconfined' means no syscall filtering is applied. 'RuntimeDefault' uses the container runtime's default profile. 'Localhost' uses a custom profile defined on the node. When privileged mode is enabled, seccomp is not enforced regardless of this setting.

lsm_profile_assigned.title: LSM Profile Assigned
lsm_profile_assigned.description: Indicates whether an AppArmor or SELinux mandatory access control profile is explicitly assigned and enforced for the container at runtime (not unconfined/disabled).

lsm_profile_mode.title: LSM Profile Enforcement Mode
lsm_profile_mode.description: The enforcement mode of the assigned LSM profile: enforcing means policies are actively blocking, permissive means policies log but do not block, unconfined means no LSM restrictions apply.

read_only_root_filesystem.title: Read-Only Root Filesystem
read_only_root_filesystem.description: Indicates whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing modification of binaries and persistent tooling installation.

network_mode.title: Container Network Mode
network_mode.description: The network mode configured for the container, determining whether it has its own network namespace or shares one with the host or another container.

host_network_enabled.title: Host Network Namespace Enabled
host_network_enabled.description: Indicates whether the container is configured to share the host's network namespace (e.g., hostNetwork: true in Kubernetes or --network=host in Docker). When true, all host network interfaces and ports are directly accessible and no container-level network boundary exists.

network_policy_enforced.title: Network Policy Enforced at Container/Pod Level
network_policy_enforced.description: Indicates whether a network policy (e.g., Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, iptables rules, CNI-enforced policy) is applied to restrict ingress/egress for this container independent of namespace isolation.

egress_network_policy_enforced.title: Egress Network Policy Enforced
egress_network_policy_enforced.description: Whether a NetworkPolicy or equivalent CNI-level egress policy is applied to the container/pod that restricts outbound connections to explicitly permitted destinations.

egress_policy_default_deny.title: Default-Deny Egress Posture
egress_policy_default_deny.description: Whether the namespace or cluster has a default-deny egress policy in place, requiring workloads to explicitly opt in to permitted egress destinations.

cni_policy_enforcement_capable.title: CNI Plugin Capable of Policy Enforcement
cni_policy_enforcement_capable.description: Whether the installed CNI plugin is capable of and configured to enforce NetworkPolicy rules (e.g., Calico, Cilium, Weave with policy, Canal). Plugins like Flannel without a policy engine cannot enforce egress rules even if policies exist.

mounted_secret_paths.title: Mounted Secret Paths
mounted_secret_paths.description: List of filesystem paths where secrets, tokens, or credentials are mounted into the container (e.g., /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount, /etc/tls, /run/secrets).

secret_mount_scope.title: Secret Mount Scope
secret_mount_scope.description: Indicates whether mounted secrets are scoped to the container's own zone or grant access to adjacent trust zones (e.g., cross-namespace service account tokens, cluster-admin credentials, wildcard TLS certificates).

read_only_secret_mounts_enforced.title: Read-Only Secret Mounts Enforced
read_only_secret_mounts_enforced.description: Whether all secret-bearing volume mounts are configured as read-only (readOnly: true). Writable secret mounts increase exposure by allowing credential modification in addition to exfiltration.

automount_service_account_token.title: Service Account Token Auto-Mounted
automount_service_account_token.description: Whether the Kubernetes service account token is automatically mounted into the container at the default path (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount). Unnecessary auto-mounting exposes API credentials even when the workload does not require API server access.

ipc_namespace_mode.title: IPC Namespace Mode
ipc_namespace_mode.description: The IPC namespace configuration for the container or pod, indicating whether it shares the host IPC namespace, a shared pod namespace, or maintains private isolation.

cross_zone_workloads_share_ipc.title: Cross-Zone Workloads Share IPC Namespace
cross_zone_workloads_share_ipc.description: Indicates whether workloads from distinct trust zones (e.g., different security tiers, tenants, or sensitivity levels) are co-located within the same IPC namespace, enabling shared memory and semaphore access across zone boundaries.

seccomp_ipc_syscalls_restricted.title: Seccomp Profile Restricts IPC Syscalls
seccomp_ipc_syscalls_restricted.description: Indicates whether an active seccomp profile blocks or restricts IPC-related syscalls (shmget, shmat, semget, semop, msgget, msgsnd, msgrcv) for the container, mitigating exploitation even when IPC namespace is shared.

syscall_auditing_enabled.title: Syscall Auditing Enabled
syscall_auditing_enabled.description: Indicates whether syscall-level auditing (e.g., auditd, seccomp audit mode) is active within or around the container runtime to capture system call activity for lateral movement detection.

ebpf_runtime_monitoring_enabled.title: eBPF-Based Runtime Monitoring Enabled
ebpf_runtime_monitoring_enabled.description: Indicates whether an eBPF-based behavioral monitoring tool (e.g., Falco with eBPF probe, Tetragon, Cilium Hubble) is deployed and actively observing container runtime behavior including network connections, file access, and process execution.

container_network_flow_logging_enabled.title: Container Network Flow Logging Enabled
container_network_flow_logging_enabled.description: Indicates whether network flow logging (e.g., CNI-level flow logs, NetworkPolicy audit logs, or Hubble flow logs) is enabled for inter-container and inter-zone traffic traversing the container boundary.

cpu_limit_enforced.title: CPU Limit Enforced
cpu_limit_enforced.description: Indicates whether a CPU limit (cgroup cpu.max or equivalent) is configured and enforced for the container, preventing unbounded CPU consumption that could degrade adjacent workloads or security controls.

memory_limit_enforced.title: Memory Limit Enforced
memory_limit_enforced.description: Indicates whether a memory limit (cgroup memory.max or equivalent) is configured and enforced for the container, preventing memory exhaustion that could degrade adjacent workloads or security controls.

pid_limit_enforced.title: PID Limit Enforced
pid_limit_enforced.description: Indicates whether a PID limit (cgroup pids.max) is configured for the container, preventing PID namespace exhaustion attacks (fork bombs) that could degrade host-level security enforcement.
